chunks: And Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The least duration of hayd is three days. If she sees blood before ten days, then it is part of the first menstruation; and if she sees it after ten days, then it is from another forthcoming menstruation.

key_terms.الدَّمَ: blood; the bleeding being legally evaluated
key_terms.الْحَيْضَةِ الْأُولَى: the first menstrual period; the original cycle to which bleeding may still belong
key_terms.الْحَيْضُ: menstruation; the legally recognized menstrual bleeding
key_terms.الْعَشَرَةِ أَيَّامٍ: ten days; the interval used to distinguish continuation from a new cycle
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةُ أَيَّامٍ: three days; the minimum duration of hayd in this ruling
key_terms.حَيْضَةٍ أُخْرَى: another menstrual period; a new cycle distinct from the previous one
key_terms.مُسْتَقْبَلَةٍ: forthcoming; meaning a newly commencing period ahead

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum duration of hayd, and when is later bleeding considered a new menstrual period?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the minimum duration of hayd and the distinction between one menstrual period and another. It states that the minimum hayd is three days, and that blood seen before ten days is counted as part of the first period, while blood seen after ten days belongs to a new menstrual cycle.
